content.title: About
content.content: Pre‑lightened coffee consists of Arabica beans that have undergone a light roast, preserving bright fruit and floral notes along with a moderate acidity. It works well for both espresso and filter brewing, delivering a balanced cup with a gentle sweetness.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Light roasting retains a high level of chlorogenic acids, which contribute to the coffee’s vivid acidity and aroma.
Arabica beans contain about 60 % more aromatic compounds than Robusta.
Pre‑lightened coffee is popular in home espresso machines because it is less prone to bitterness from under‑extraction.
In some cultures the first cup of light‑roasted coffee is served as a ceremonial welcome.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Coffee provides polyphenols that help combat free radicals and reduce oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports cognitive function
items.content: Caffeine improves alertness, memory, and reaction time, especially when consumed in moderate amounts.

items.title: Boosts metabolism
items.content: Caffeine can increase energy expenditure, contributing to a higher basal metabolic rate.

items.title: Contains magnesium and potassium
items.content: These minerals are essential for muscle function, nerve signaling, and fluid balance.

items.title: May lower risk of certain diseases
items.content: Regular moderate coffee consumption is associated with a reduced risk of Parkinson’s disease and some cancers.

items.title: Caffeine sensitivity
items.content: Some individuals may experience anxiety, insomnia, or rapid heartbeat with excessive intake.

items.title: Increased stomach acidity
items.content: Coffee can aggravate gastritis or reflux symptoms in susceptible people.

items.title: Drug interactions
items.content: Caffeine may amplify the effects of certain stimulants and diminish the efficacy of some sedatives.

content.title: How to Prepare
content.content: For pre‑lightened coffee, use a medium grind for filter brewing and a finer grind for espresso. Brew 18‑20 g of coffee with 300 ml of water at 92‑96 °C, steeping for 2‑3 minutes. Add milk, cream, or spices to taste if desired.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store coffee in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. Keep it away from air, moisture, and light to preserve flavor and aroma. Once opened, use within 2‑3 weeks for optimal freshness.

content.title: About
content.content: Dove is a well‑known skin‑care brand celebrated for its gentle, nourishing formulas. The fried version (947) is a scented cream‑paste that is lightly toasted to a golden crust while retaining the beneficial properties of the original product.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Dove was launched in 1957 by Unilever.
The fried (947) edition was introduced in 2023 as a limited‑edition release.
The product contains 5 % natural shea butter, which helps lock in moisture.
Packaging is made from recyclable plastic, reducing environmental impact.
Its flavor combines a subtle caramel note with a gentle lavender aroma.

items.title: Moisturizing
items.content: Shea butter and glycerin work together to retain water in the outer skin layers.

items.title: Soothing
items.content: Mild emulsifiers reduce the risk of irritation, even for sensitive skin.

items.title: Antioxidant effect
items.content: Vitamins E and C in the formula help combat free radicals.

items.title: Calming scent
items.content: Lavender in the fragrance promotes relaxation and stress relief.

items.title: Barrier support
items.content: Lipids strengthen the skin’s natural barrier, protecting against moisture loss.

items.title: Allergy to ingredients
items.content: Contains shea butter and fragrance components that may cause allergic reactions.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: The cream’s oil content makes it relatively calorie‑dense; use in moderation.

items.title: Not for children under 3
items.content: Texture may pose a choking hazard for very young children.

items.title: Eye contact
items.content: May cause irritation if it gets into the eyes; rinse thoroughly with water.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Apply a small amount to clean facial or body skin, gently massage until fully absorbed. For an extra boost, combine with other Dove products.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. Once opened, use within 12 months. Discard if the smell or color changes.

content.title: About
content.content: Pompano (Pampus argenteus) is a marine fish from the jack family, native to warm coastal waters of the Indo‑Pacific region. Grilled fillet offers a delicate, slightly sweet flavor, firm yet tender texture, and a subtle smoky aroma.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pompano is often called the “golden sea perch” because of its golden‑hued flesh.
The species can change sex during its life; young males may become females later on.
In China, pompano is considered a delicacy and frequently appears on upscale restaurant menus.
It grows quickly, reaching up to 60 cm and 2 kg within a year.
Pompano is commonly farmed in aquaculture, reducing pressure on wild stocks.

items.title: Rich in omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Omega‑3s support heart health, reduce inflammation, and aid brain function.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Easily digestible fish protein helps build and repair muscle tissue.

items.title: Source of vitamin D
items.content: Vitamin D is essential for bone health, immune function, and calcium regulation.

items.title: Contains selenium
items.content: Selenium acts as a powerful antioxidant and supports thyroid health.

items.title: Low mercury levels
items.content: Compared with larger predatory fish, pompano has low mercury, making it safe for regular consumption.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to seafood, including pompano.

items.title: Possible contaminants
items.content: Like any marine fish, pompano can contain trace pollutants (e.g., PCBs); purchase from reputable sources.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: When grilled with added salt, sodium levels can rise; people with hypertension should monitor salt intake.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve grilled pompano fillet hot, drizzled with lemon juice or an olive‑oil‑based sauce. It pairs well with vegetable sides, quinoa, rice, or fresh green salads.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cooked fillet in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 2‑3 days. For longer storage, freeze in a bag at –18 °C; thaw in the fridge before serving.

content.title: About
content.content: Mixed nuts, without peanuts, unsalted is a blend of selected nuts (almonds, cashews, hazelnuts, walnuts, pine nuts and others) with no added salt and no peanuts. The nuts are rich in healthy fats, protein, vitamins and minerals, making them an excellent snack and ingredient for many dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Nut mixes are often used in cooking to create varied flavors and textures.
The absence of peanuts makes the product safer for people allergic to peanuts, though it still poses a risk for those allergic to other nuts.
The unsalted version preserves the natural taste and nutritional profile of the nuts.
Nuts in the mix can be raw or lightly roasted, depending on the manufacturer.
Mixed nuts are a popular choice for athletes because of their high protein and energy content.

items.title: Rich in healthy fats
items.content: Nuts contain monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fatty acids that support heart health.

items.title: Source of plant protein
items.content: The blend provides a substantial amount of protein important for tissue repair.

items.title: Contains vitamin E
items.content: Vitamin E acts as a powerful antioxidant protecting cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: High in minerals
items.content: Nuts supply magnesium, phosphorus, zinc and iron, essential for many biochemical processes.

items.title: Promotes satiety
items.content: Fiber and protein in nuts help maintain a feeling of fullness longer.

items.title: Tree nut allergy
items.content: The mix can trigger allergic reactions in individuals sensitive to any of the included nuts.

items.title: High in calories
items.content: Nuts are calorie-dense, so portion size should be moderated.

items.title: Choking hazard
items.content: Whole nuts may pose a choking risk for young children.

items.title: Oxalate content
items.content: Some nuts (e.g., almonds) contain oxalates, which may contribute to kidney stone formation in susceptible people.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Unsalted mixed nuts without peanuts are convenient as a standalone snack, added to granola, yogurt, salads, baked goods, or used in sauces. They can be lightly toasted to enhance flavor if desired.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the nuts in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. For longer shelf life, keep them in the refrigerator or freezer to prevent fat oxidation. Discard nuts that smell rancid or stale.

content.title: About
content.content: Moose is a smooth, creamy dessert made from milk, cream, sugar and flavorings. It has a delicate texture and a light sweet taste, often served chilled in individual cups.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first commercial moose was created in the early 20th century in France.
There are more than twenty moose flavors, including chocolate, fruit, caramel and herbal.
Moose is popular in culinary shows because it can be molded into elegant shapes.
Traditional French moose is made with whipped egg whites, giving it an airy consistency.

items.title: Calcium source
items.content: Milk‑based moose provides calcium, essential for bone health.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Dairy ingredients supply protein that supports tissue repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: It contains vitamins B2 and B12, which aid energy metabolism.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: People with lactose intolerance should choose lactose‑free versions.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Sweet varieties can contribute to weight gain if consumed in excess.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Traditional moose often contains egg whites, which may trigger allergic reactions.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve moose chilled in individual cups, garnish with berries, mint or chocolate shavings. It can also be used as a layer in cakes and dessert parfaits.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep moose refrigerated at 2‑4 °C in a sealed container for up to 3 days. Discard if it develops a sour smell or off‑color.

content.title: About
content.content: Fruit pancakes are thin, pan‑fried cakes made from a batter of flour, eggs, milk, and a touch of sugar, topped or folded with fresh or canned fruit. They have a delicate texture, a mildly sweet aroma, and a juicy fruit filling.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pancakes are a traditional staple in Russia and Eastern Europe, and fruit‑filled versions have become popular worldwide for their taste and nutrition.
More than 30 fruit varieties are commonly used: strawberry, banana, blueberry, raspberry, kiwi, and others.
Pancakes can be served sweet or savory; fruit pancakes are usually accompanied by sour cream, yogurt, or honey.
Thin pancakes cook in 1–2 minutes per side, making them a quick breakfast option.

items.title: Rich in vitamins
items.content: Fruits in the filling provide vitamin C, vitamin A, and folate, supporting immunity and vision.

items.title: Source of fiber
items.content: Fruit and whole‑grain flour add dietary fiber that promotes healthy digestion.

items.title: Low glycemic impact
items.content: Thin whole‑grain pancakes cause a slower rise in blood sugar compared with regular white‑flour pancakes.

items.title: Energy boost
items.content: The combination of carbohydrates from the batter and natural fruit sugars quickly replenishes energy stores.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Berries such as blueberries and raspberries are high in antioxidants that protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Fruit allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to certain fruits like strawberries or kiwi.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Fruit pancakes can contain a lot of natural sugar; people with diabetes should monitor portion size.

items.title: Heat‑related compounds
items.content: Over‑cooking pancakes may produce acrylamide, a potentially harmful compound.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve fruit pancakes hot, rolled or folded, drizzled with honey, yogurt, maple syrup, or dusted with powdered sugar. They make a great breakfast or light dessert.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cooked pancakes in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. Freeze in a single layer separated by parchment if you need longer storage (up to 2 months). Reheat gently with a splash of water to prevent drying out.

content.title: About
content.content: Pork and vegetables is a dish where tender pieces of pork are stir‑fried with a variety of vegetables such as bell pepper, zucchini, mushrooms and onion. The recipe excludes carrots, broccoli, dark‑green leafy greens, potatoes and soy‑based sauce, making it lighter and suitable for those avoiding these ingredients.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pork is one of the most widely consumed meats worldwide and is rich in protein.
Traditional Asian cuisine often uses soy sauce, but this version replaces it with aromatic herbs and spices.
Vegetables like bell pepper and zucchini are high in vitamin C and antioxidants.
Quick stir‑frying preserves the juiciness of the meat and the crisp texture of the vegetables.
The dish can be easily adapted to different cuisines by changing the spice blend (e.g., adding paprika or ginger).

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Pork provides all essential amino acids needed for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Pork is a good source of B1, B3 and B6 vitamins, which support energy metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: The dish supplies iron, zinc and selenium, important for immune function and skin health.

items.title: Antioxidants from vegetables
items.content: Bell pepper and zucchini contain carotenoids and vitamin C that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Low in carbohydrates
items.content: Excluding potatoes and soy sauce makes the meal suitable for low‑carb diets.

items.title: Undercooked pork
items.content: Insufficiently cooked pork may harbor harmful bacteria; cook to an internal temperature of 71 °C (160 °F).

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: If soy sauce is replaced with salt, monitor the amount to avoid excessive sodium intake.

items.title: Allergy to spices
items.content: Some individuals may be sensitive to spices used as soy‑sauce alternatives (e.g., mustard).

items.title: High fat content
items.content: Choosing leaner cuts of pork (such as tenderloin) helps reduce overall saturated fat.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the dish hot, paired with whole‑grain rice, quinoa, or simply as a standalone meal. Leftover vegetables can be added to a cold salad, or the mixture can be used as a filling for wraps.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked pork and vegetables in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. When frozen, the dish keeps well for up to 2 months; thaw in the fridge before reheating.

content.title: About
content.content: Ryazhenka is a fermented dairy drink made from baked milk that is soured with lactic acid cultures. It has a delicate creamy color, a slightly sweet caramel-like flavor, and a mild tang. Ryazhenka is drunk cold, added to batter for pancakes and fritters, and used in baking and desserts.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Ryazhenka is a traditional drink of the Eastern Slavs, popular in Ukraine, Russia, and Belarus.
The milk for ryazhenka is simmered for a long time at high heat until it takes on a creamy color and caramel flavor.
The fat content of ryazhenka is usually 2.5 to 4 percent.
Ryazhenka differs from kefir and yogurt in that it is made from baked milk.
Good ryazhenka contains live lactic acid cultures.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: Calcium is needed for bones and teeth.

items.title: Contains protein
items.content: Milk protein supports muscles and helps you feel full.

items.title: Contains vitamin B12 and riboflavin
items.content: These vitamins support metabolism and the formation of blood cells.

items.title: Contains lactic acid bacteria
items.content: Live cultures in fermented foods support gut microflora.

items.title: Slightly less lactose
items.content: During fermentation some of the lactose is broken down, so some people tolerate it better than milk.

items.title: Lactose
items.content: Ryazhenka contains lactose, so it may not suit people with lactose intolerance.

items.title: Milk allergy
items.content: Ryazhenka is not suitable for people with an allergy to cow's milk proteins.

items.title: Sugar and additives
items.content: Sweetened and flavored versions may contain a lot of added sugar.

items.title: Fat content
items.content: Ryazhenka is fattier than kefir, so portions should be moderate, especially with high cholesterol.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Drink ryazhenka cold, at breakfast or as a snack, add it to smoothies, and use it to make pancakes, fritters, baking batter, and desserts. It is better to choose ryazhenka without added sugar.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store ryazhenka in the refrigerator in a closed package and use it before the expiration date; after opening, within two to three days. Freezing is not recommended. Discard ryazhenka that is moldy or has an unusual smell.

content.title: About
content.content: Tortilla chips are crunchy slices made from corn tortillas that are fried or baked until golden. The Doritos line offers a wide range of flavors, from classic cheese to spicy and aromatic blends such as chili‑lime, taco, and barbecue.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first commercial Doritos brand was launched in the United States in 1966 by Frito‑Lay.
In 1972 the iconic "Nacho Cheese" flavor was introduced and became the best‑selling variety worldwide.
There are more than 30 permanent Doritos flavors, plus seasonal limited‑edition releases.
Tortilla chips are made from whole‑grain corn, making them naturally gluten‑free.
In some markets Doritos are sold as "stacks" – thicker, softer pieces rather than traditional chips.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: Corn chips provide carbohydrates that quickly supply the body with energy, making them a convenient snack before physical activity.

items.title: Contains fiber
items.content: Whole‑grain corn contributes a modest amount of dietary fiber, supporting digestive health.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Certain flavors, such as tomato or pepper blends, contain natural antioxidants from spices.

items.title: Gluten‑free
items.content: Made from pure corn, tortilla chips are suitable for people with gluten intolerance.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Corn provides thiamine, niacin, and folate, which play roles in metabolism.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Many Doritos flavors contain a notable amount of salt, which can raise blood pressure if consumed frequently.

items.title: Fat and calorie density
items.content: Fried chips are high in fats and calories, so they should be eaten in moderation, especially for weight management.

items.title: Allergens
items.content: Some varieties contain dairy, soy, or spice ingredients that may trigger allergic reactions.

items.title: Trans fats
items.content: Products made with partially hydrogenated oils may contain trans fats, which are detrimental to heart health.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Tortilla chips are perfect as a standalone snack, tossed into salads, paired with guacamole or salsa, or used as a base for loaded nachos. They pair well with cheese, beans, vegetables, and a variety of dips.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep chips in the original package or an airtight container in a cool, dry place. For longer shelf life, store them in the refrigerator to maintain crunchiness and prevent fat oxidation.
